findings.title: apply_ledger widened so one waiver can silently disable a sibling rule's enforcement
locations: test/scans.jl: "a policy waiver on any rule a scan enforces disables it"
findings.before:
id = row["id"]; rule = row["rule"]
    for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")
        e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)
    end
findings.after:
id = row["id"]
    enforced = unique!(vcat(String(row["rule"]), rules_for_scan(id)))
    for rule in enforced, e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy")
        e["target"] == "*" && return (Hit[], length(hits), true)
    end
findings.why_it_matters: A consumer who already has an existing `.gbg/exemptions.toml` entry — `RULE.CIT.DOI, scope = "policy", target = "*"` — with no code change on their side, moves from "this entry does nothing" (base behaviour) to "this entry disables the whole SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK scan", which also silently stops enforcing RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE for them, a check that was previously live and gating their build. This is precisely the audit's target shape — a change to a computed result (scan hits go from present to silently exempted) for previously valid ledger input, announced only in an internal Julia docstring and a unit test, not in CHANGELOG.md or any consumer-facing policy text, so a ledger author who set the DOI waiver believing (correctly, at base) that it was a no-op has no way to learn their FULL_INLINE enforcement just went dark.
findings.description: The claimed defect was narrow — a documented, accepted `RULE.CIT.DOI` waiver had zero effect because apply_ledger only checked the scan's single catalogue-canonical rule. The fix is correct for that direction (the waiver now has an effect) but is implemented as "disable the entire scan on a hit against ANY rule it enforces", which is wider than the defect requires: it also makes a rule that scan enforces but that the consumer never exempted (FULL_INLINE) silently stop being enforced whenever the sibling rule (DOI) carries a target-`*` policy waiver, since Hit carries no rule id to filter by. The docstring names this as a known, deliberately un-fixed limitation rather than treating it as an open defect, so the change was shipped as a widened contract by design, not by oversight — but the widening is still real, silent to the exemptions-ledger author, and never called out in the fix as something requiring re-review of existing ledgers.
findings.evidence: src/Scan.jl docstring added in this diff: "The mirror case is NOT fixed and is a known limit: a waiver on either rule still disables the WHOLE scan, so it withdraws enforcement of a sibling rule the consumer never exempted. A `Hit` carries no rule id, so the engine cannot drop one rule's hits and keep the other's." Confirmed by test/scans.jl: "r = G.run_scan(d, row; ledger = pol("RULE.CIT.DOI")); @test isempty(r.hits) && r.exempted > 0  # the waiver that was void".

findings.title: gbg round close now refuses check-docs/check-consistency rounds with no recorded build, rejecting a previously-successful invocation
findings.before: close() had no build-verdict check at all; a round with no `gbg round build` ever run, or one that ran and returned nonzero, could still close as long as the other conditions (dirty files, pass budget, dead lanes, config sha) were met.
findings.after:
if inst in Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS
        b = get(rec, "build", nothing)
        if b === nothing
            push!(fails, "no docs build is recorded for this round — gbg round build $round")
        elseif b["code"] != 0
            push!(fails, "the recorded docs build exited $(b["code"]) — fix it, then gbg round build $round")
findings.why_it_matters: Any check-docs/check-consistency round that was opened before this change and never had `gbg round build` run against it (which was a legal, closing-eligible state at base) will now fail `close` with a new refusal until the operator runs the new verb. This is exactly the fix's intended effect and is well announced in the schema description and inline comments, so it is disclosed, but it is still a behaviour change to an existing CLI verb's exit-code contract for input that used to succeed.
findings.description: The refusal is scoped tightly to the two instruments that actually build docs (via the same Sync.DOCS_INSTRUMENTS constant used elsewhere), matches the concrete defect described (a RED build riding through graded passes to close), and is thoroughly documented in the schema, the docstring and inline comments — including a staleness check reusing the existing audit_after_code pattern rather than inventing a new one. Flagged for completeness per the lens brief (a previously-working `gbg round close` invocation can now exit 2), not because the change looks unjustified.
findings.evidence: schema/round.schema.json new field description: "Nothing recorded a build's verdict before 2026-09-12, so a round could carry a RED build through graded passes and close on it: `prepare` builds green at open, a fix pass's prose edits move SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE's ratchet, and neither `pass open` nor `grade` looks at a build again." test/rounds.jl had to add "build" => Dict(...) to three previously-passing close() fixtures to keep them passing, confirming the new requirement is enforced against prior test data.

findings.title: gbg round prepare now refuses on any partially-unanchored seed catalogue, rejecting a previously-tolerated invocation
findings.before:
plan, skipped = Seeds.select(cat, f, rec["seed_salt"])
            f2, s2 = Seeds.plant(f, s, plan)
            write(full, f2); write(site, s2)
            println(io, "prepare: $(length(plan)) seed(s) planted (salt $(rec["seed_salt"]))", isempty(skipped) ? "" : "; skipped classes (anchor absent): " * join(skipped, ", "))
findings.after:
if !isempty(skipped)
                println(io, "prepare: refused — $(length(skipped)) seed class(es) have no anchor in the manuscript: ", join(skipped, ", "))
                return 2
            end
            f2, s2 = Seeds.plant(f, s, plan)
findings.why_it_matters: A round whose seed catalogue plants most, but not all, classes previously prepared successfully (with a warning line naming the skipped classes) and produced a round that measured recall over fewer classes than the catalogue names. That invocation now refuses outright (exit 2) until the catalogue is re-anchored or `--no-seed` is passed. Operators relying on the old "warn and continue" behaviour for a catalogue they haven't fully maintained will see a new hard failure where there was none before.
findings.description: The change targets a real, named defect (a class with a rotted anchor reads as UNDEFINED and silently shrinks the recall denominator, exactly the failure mode that let a 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 seed go unmeasured) and is symmetric across both docs-round paths that plant seeds. It does reject previously-tolerated input, which the lens asks to be surfaced, but the narrowing is proportionate to the defect (a partially-plantable catalogue is precisely the case that made the recall metric silently unreliable) rather than over-broad.
findings.evidence: src/CLI/Rounds.jl comment on the added block: "the same refusal the docs path makes: a class that cannot plant leaves recall UNDEFINED for it and quietly narrows the denominator, which reads as a smaller catalogue rather than a broken one."
